items.q: What did the on-stage outfit change prove?
items.a: **Image is powerful and superficial.** Six seconds in a sweater rewrote what the room thought of her. Most people cannot run that transform. The pictures are **constructions** — hair, makeup, crew, pre/post — not the girl in the grandma or soccer photo. First bikini shoot: **before she had her period.**

items.q: What is the honest answer to 'how do you become a model?'
items.a: Not 'I was scouted.' **Genetic lottery + a beauty legacy** (tall, slender, feminine, white) she is cashing out. 2007 NYU count: **677 hired, 27 non-white (<4%)**. Wanting to model is **Powerball**, not a path. Tell the kid to be the editor or CEO.

items.q: What free stuff does Russell say we don't like to talk about?
items.a: Not the 8-inch heels. Cambridge store **gave her the dress** when she forgot money. Teenage red light: **'Sorry, officer'** and they drove on. **How she looks, not who she is.** Inverse: NYC **140k** teen stop-and-frisks, **86% Black and Latino**, vs ~**177k** young Black and Latino men in the city — frequency, not whether.

items.q: Will thinner thighs and shinier hair make you happier?
items.a: Meet the models. They have the target and are **the most physically insecure**. She has never said on camera: **I am insecure**, because the job is thinking about how you look every day. US girls: **53%** dislike their bodies at 13, **78%** by 17.

items.q: What is the takeaway she wants?
items.a: Get more comfortable acknowledging the **power of image in perceived successes and perceived failures**. She is uncomfortable both naming the stacked deck and saying it does not always make her happy — and more uncomfortable unpacking oppression as one of its biggest beneficiaries.
